text.approach: Drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) to Hannegan Pass Road (FS 32); at 1.3 miles bear left onto Ruth Creek Road and continue to a pullout near milepost 3, just past a creek flowing over a concrete weir (about 2,950 ft), well short of the road's end at Hannegan Campground. From the pullout, cross Ruth Creek (a log crossing has been used) and bushwhack roughly 45 minutes through slide alder and devil's club to the base of the Wall Street couloir.

text.overview: The classic north-side line: a steep snow gully ('Wall Street') gains the Northwest Glacier, which is crossed to a 6,500-ft saddle west of the summit, followed by a Class 2-3 scramble up the exposed southeast ridge to the top.
text.descent: Reverse the southeast-ridge scramble to the 6,500-ft saddle, re-cross the Northwest Glacier, and plunge-step down the roughly 1,500-ft Wall Street couloir back to the bushwhack and Ruth Creek crossing.

text.overview: Lichen and loose rock mar parts of this bigger outing, which adds roughly 1200 feet and sustained 5.9+ cracks to the regular North Ridge. Easy fifth class follows the crest above the hardest early pitches, which include a slot and a long layback crack past a small roof. Bivouac sites sit around 8200 feet at the notch. Time varies enormously: a rapid half-day simul-climbing, or several days if pitched out.

text.overview: Crack and corner route. P1 (5.11- or 5.10+): hand and finger splitter from a small ledge to a broad ledge, then a mantle and a yellow corner. P2 (5.9): leftward through hanging corners and arete turns to a bolted ledge. P3 (5.10+): face holds to a 4 inch crack and a slung horn near big orange roofs, then diagonal cracks right; may be easier as two pitches. P4 (5.10-): finger cracks and stemming.
